Claude Desktop (the Claude app)

Set up the Claude app (Claude Desktop) with GateFox: first setup, switching configurations, SSH environments on other Macs, and what the gateway does for it.

About 13 min read · 9 sections

On this page
01 Set it up 02 SSH environments 03 Model IDs 04 What the gateway does for these IDs 05 Endpoints 06 Claude Code model discovery 07 Moving from the adapter 08 Limits 09 Verification

GateFox shows every model it serves in the Claude app's model picker: your Claude accounts first, then Codex accounts, local models and API models. The app talks to the gateway on this Mac directly; nothing else is installed.

Claude Desktop refuses a model ID that names GPT or Qwen, so it cannot name gateway aliases such as codex/gpt-6.1-sol. Until now a separate loopback adapter translated Claude-safe IDs into aliases. The gateway now resolves those IDs itself, so the app can connect to the same listener Codex and Claude Code use.

before   Claude Desktop → adapter :3467 → (private inference) → gateway → providers
direct   Claude Desktop ──────────────────────────────────────→ gateway → providers

There is no adapter process, no second gateway configuration, no extra port and no LiteLLM-style proxy. Every model the gateway's catalog shows becomes one picker row with its real provider and model label, such as Claude · Opus 5.5, Claude 2 · Opus 5.5 or Codex · GPT-6.1-Sol.

Set it up

You need GateFox running on this Mac (gateway doctor passes) and the Claude app installed.

  1. Create a configuration named GateFox in the Claude app, once. Open the app's third-party configuration window (Developer → Configure Third-Party Inference…; see Anthropic's in-app configuration guide). Set Inference provider to Gateway, the gateway base URL to http://127.0.0.1:3457, name the configuration GateFox, and apply it. The next step fills in everything else. A configuration still named Harness Gateway is also accepted and renamed.

  2. Quit the Claude app (⌘Q), then write the GateFox settings:

    gateway claude-desktop configure --direct --apply

  3. Open the Claude app. The account menu at the bottom left reads you · GateFox, and the model picker lists your Claude accounts first.

Without --apply the command only writes a candidate for review. It reads the gateway's model list and writes a candidate profile to ~/Library/Application Support/Claude-3p/alias-trial/candidate/desktop-profile.json. Review it, finish Claude work, quit the app, and apply:

gateway claude-desktop configure --direct --apply

--apply replaces only the selected profile, after writing a private backup under Claude-3p/setup-backups, and refuses to run while Claude is open. It sets the gateway origin, the credential helper, and the model rows. Unrelated profile settings are kept. Run the command again after you add, remove or hide models in the gateway; the picker does not refresh by itself.

Option Effect
--gateway-config PATH Uses that gateway configuration for the port and client token. The default is the installed configuration.
--endpoint URL --token-file PATH Names a gateway reached through a loopback SSH forward. Only its public model list is read.
--tailnet Names this Mac's Tailscale HTTPS address, https://NAME.ts.net:PORT, instead of 127.0.0.1. Needed for SSH environments.
--ssh-host HOST With --tailnet, adds the host to the profile's sshHostAllowlist. Repeat it, or separate hosts with commas.
--model ID_OR_ALIAS Lists that model first, by row ID or gateway alias. Without it, the model the profile already starts with stays first.
--native-model-metadata Writes opaque row IDs with behavesAs, for an app version that reads it. See native model metadata.

--port and --primary-claude-provider belong to the adapter profile and are refused with --direct.

Rows are listed Claude accounts first: the primary Claude account, then the other Claude accounts, then every other provider in the gateway's catalog order.

On a Claude app that reads native model metadata (5.1231 or later was checked), add --native-model-metadata so Codex and other reasoning rows show the app's own effort control.

Switch configurations

The Claude app keeps third-party configurations and their chats separately from your normal Claude sign-in, under ~/Library/Application Support/Claude-3p. Switch between configurations from the account menu: Inference configuration, choose one, then Apply Changes. Every --apply keeps the previous profile in Claude-3p/setup-backups.

SSH environments

Claude Desktop can run a Code session's Claude Code engine on another machine over SSH, while the window stays on this Mac. With a third-party profile such as GateFox, two rules from Anthropic decide whether that works (SSH remote sessions on 3P):

  1. SSH stays off, and New environment offers no SSH tab, until the profile sets sshHostAllowlist.
  2. The remote engine calls the profile's endpoint from the remote host, with the token the credential helper prints on this Mac. Claude Desktop refuses a loopback endpoint (localhost, *.localhost, 127.x, ::1, 0.0.0.0) for those sessions with "SSH sessions can't use your model provider settings". It checks the literal name only, and resolves nothing.
  3. Every other endpoint must use https://. The app accepts plain http:// only on loopback, and its configuration window drops any other http:// URL when it saves.

Codex's SSH support carries the gateway inside its own SSH connection. Claude Desktop owns its SSH connection and opens no tunnel for inference, so the gateway must answer on an address the host can reach, over HTTPS. With tailnetListener the gateway also listens on this Mac's own Tailscale addresses, with TLS and this Mac's Tailscale certificate:

local session   Claude Desktop ─────────────────────────────► https://NAME.ts.net:3457 ─┐
SSH session     Claude Desktop ══SSH══► host: Claude Code ───► https://NAME.ts.net:3457 ─┴► this Mac's GateFox

The gateway fetches the certificate itself with tailscale cert: a Let's Encrypt certificate for this Mac's MagicDNS name, which Tailscale renews. The gateway asks for it again every 12 hours and serves a renewed one to new connections without rebinding. Tailscale prints the pair to standard output and the gateway keeps it in memory only; nothing is written to disk, which also suits the sandboxed App Store build of Tailscale. The tailnet must allow HTTPS certificates (Tailscale admin console → DNS → HTTPS Certificates). Without a certificate the tailnet listener stays closed and records tailnet_listener with state certificate_unavailable; it retries every five minutes.

Both kinds of session use this Mac's gateway, its accounts and its model list, as a Codex SSH chat does.

Set it up

You need Tailscale on this Mac and on the host, with MagicDNS and HTTPS Certificates turned on for the tailnet (Tailscale admin console → DNS). Both the standalone and the App Store build of Tailscale work. Check that ssh HOST already works from a terminal on this Mac.

  1. Add "tailnetListener": true to the gateway configuration. The running gateway fetches its certificate and starts listening within about a minute, without a restart, on the same port.

  2. Quit the Claude app, then write the profile. Name each host both by the alias you type in the app and by the address that alias resolves to (ssh -G HOST | grep '^hostname'), because the app checks the resolved address:

    gateway claude-desktop configure --direct --tailnet \
  --ssh-host macbook-server --ssh-host 100.73.86.17 --apply

  3. Open the Claude app. Choose the environment selector under the prompt box, then New environment → SSH → Host → Add SSH connection…:

    Field Value
    Host the alias from ~/.ssh/config, such as macbook-server
    User your user on the host, or blank when the SSH config sets it
    SSH key the IdentityFile that ssh -G HOST prints. Press ⌘⇧. in the file picker to show .ssh

    Accept the host key, choose a folder on the host and select Create environment.

To add a host later, run step 2 again with every host listed.

The host needs the Claude Code engine's own requirements and a route to this Mac over Tailscale; it needs no GateFox. --ssh-host entries are hostnames, *.domain wildcards or IP addresses, matched against the HostName that ~/.ssh/config gives for the entered host. * is refused, because every listed host receives the gateway token for the session. Without --ssh-host, an allowlist already in the profile is kept.

What the tailnet listener accepts

Check Behavior
Addresses This Mac's non-internal addresses in 100.64.0.0/10 and fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48, rechecked every 30 seconds, so an address that appears after login is picked up and one that leaves is closed.
Peers Only Tailscale addresses. Any other peer is closed before the TLS handshake.
Transport TLS 1.2 or later with this Mac's Tailscale certificate. Plain HTTP is not served there.
Requests Handed to the loopback listener's own HTTP server: the same client token, the browser-origin refusal, admission limits and timeouts. Only GET /health answers without the token, as on loopback.
Upgrades An in-place upgrade keeps the sockets and reconciles them with the configuration it adopts. Setting the key to false, or removing it, closes them.

Every tailnet device can reach the port, and any device holding the client token can use every account this gateway serves. Turn the listener on only on Macs whose SSH sessions need it, and issue the token only to machines you trust.

The profile names the MagicDNS name, which stays the same when the Tailscale address changes. If the Mac or the tailnet is renamed, run the configure command again. Each listener start records a tailnet_listener telemetry event with the number of addresses served, not the addresses themselves.

Model IDs

The gateway derives the IDs from each alias alone, with the same function the adapter profile uses, so an ID is stable for as long as its alias exists.

Row ID the app sends Resolves to
Model of the primary Claude account Its own ID, such as claude-fable-5-1 The gateway's bare-name routing
Any other route with reasoning levels claude-opus-5[hg-route-<n>], or claude-hg-route-<n> with behavesAs That alias
Any other route without reasoning levels claude-hg-route-<n> That alias

An ID is another spelling of one fixed alias. It never selects a different account, and a failed request is never moved to another model. The gateway also accepts the hidden effort and speed aliases that earlier adapter profiles listed, so a chat saved against an adapter profile continues when the adapter used the same gateway aliases.

The primary Claude account is the one marked defaultForBareModels, or the only Claude subscription when there is exactly one. With two Claude accounts and no designation, no account keeps native IDs: every Claude model is listed as a route row with its account label, and Auto mode has no reviewer (see auto mode). Mark one account to keep its native rows:

{ "id": "claude-primary", "type": "claude-subscription", "defaultForBareModels": true }

That setting also decides which account serves a bare Claude model name from any other client, so set it deliberately.

What the gateway does for these IDs

The behavior matches the adapter and applies only to a request that names a Claude-safe ID. A request that names an alias is handled as before.

  • The reply carries the ID the client named.
  • A reasoning effort the route does not offer is lowered to the highest offered level below it, or raised to the lowest one. The gateway never adds an effort the client did not send.
  • An auxiliary review keeps its own generation controls.
  • For codex-subscription and responses-api routes, optional tool properties are sent as nullable, and only the nulls introduced that way are removed from returned tool arguments. See tools and subagents.
  • A row the catalog hides is not listed, but its ID still resolves.

Each resolved request records a claude_direct_route telemetry event with the alias and whether a hidden variant was used. It contains no request content.

Endpoints

Endpoint Behavior
GET /v1/models with an anthropic-version or x-api-key header Returns the Anthropic model list: one row per visible model, with a gatefox object holding the alias, the offered efforts, and the bridge ID.
GET /v1/models without those headers Returns the alias list, unchanged.
GET /v1/models/{id} Returns one model by row ID, bridge ID or hidden alias. An unknown ID is a 404 in the Anthropic error envelope.
POST /v1/messages Resolves a Claude-safe ID as described above.

POST /v1/responses does not accept these IDs.

Claude Code model discovery

Claude Code can fill /model from a gateway when CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY=1 is set next to ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. It keeps only IDs that contain claude or anthropic, which is why it used to hide every GPT and local model here. The Anthropic list above passes that filter, so discovery now returns one row per gateway model, with its real label.

The generated settings remain the better setup for Claude Code. They list the gateway aliases themselves and declare the launch model's context window and default effort. A discovered row is an ID Claude Code does not know, so it assumes a 200K window for it.

When it does not connect

Message in the app Cause Fix
New environment shows no SSH tab The profile has no sshHostAllowlist Run step 2 with --ssh-host
"SSH host "100.x.y.z" is not allowed by your organization's managed settings" Only the alias, not its resolved address, is listed Add the address with another --ssh-host
"Some saved settings can't be used as written: inferenceGatewayBaseUrl" The profile has a non-loopback http:// endpoint, written by 1.9.3 Choose Cancel, not Save; quit the app and run step 2 again on 1.9.6 or later
"SSH sessions can't use your model provider settings" The profile still names 127.0.0.1 Run step 2; it needs --tailnet
configure says the gateway does not answer on https://… The tailnet listener has no certificate yet Check HTTPS Certificates in the tailnet, then wait a minute; gateway diagnostics shows tailnet_listener certificate_unavailable meanwhile

Moving from the adapter

Apply a direct profile as shown above. The adapter configuration on disk and a running adapter component are left as they are, so the previous profile in setup-backups still works if you restore it. An idle adapter can stay until you retire it; nothing connects to it once the profile names the gateway.

If the adapter pointed at a different gateway configuration with different alias names, the opaque IDs differ, and a chat saved against the old profile asks you to choose a model again.

Limits

  • Claude Desktop shows its effort control only for a model ID it recognizes, or for a row with behavesAs on an app version that reads it. Fast mode and Ultracode are not offered to third-party profiles by the unmodified app.
  • The app estimates the context window from the model ID, not from the list. A mapped route inherits a 1M estimate; see the compaction limitation.
  • The profile holds at most 200 rows. The command reports the count and fails instead of dropping a model.
  • A catalog that would need more than 1000 hidden effort and speed aliases keeps its rows and drops only those hidden aliases.
  • Managed routing aliases (managed/...) are not listed.
  • Claude's mobile Remote Control does not accept a custom gateway, and the Claude mobile app has no setting for one. Gateway models reach a phone through the ChatGPT app and the native relay.

Verification

On 11 November 2026 the native Claude Code CLI 2.1.299 completed six turns against a real gateway listener with no adapter, using a synthetic loopback backend. Bridge rows and opaque rows with behavesAs both reached their own upstream model. A max request reached a route that offers up to high as high, and medium reached a low/high route as low. In the sixth run the settings held no picker rows: the client's own gateway discovery kept both listed rows, and a turn on a discovered ID completed. See the sanitized receipt.

npm run build
node scripts/e2e-claude-direct.mjs --claude /absolute/path/to/claude

This check uses no account and no paid inference.

In the app, on 11 and 12 November 2026 (Claude Desktop 4.23118 and 5.1231.2): the picker listed the direct profile's rows with Claude accounts first, and a real Claude Opus 5.5 turn sent from the app window completed. Real turns on Claude, Claude 2 and Codex rows completed through the same endpoint. With tailnetListener, another Mac reached the HTTPS endpoint with certificate verification, was refused without the client token, and could not reach plain HTTP there. A complete turn in an SSH environment, the /model picker after discovery, and Auto mode through a direct profile have not been recorded yet.

The adapter profile is the earlier setup; it stays supported for existing installations.
